title: Valid Conv1d
summary: A one-channel, valid 1D cross-correlation applies a three-tap learned filter to a five-value signal and adds one output-channel bias.
formula: y[n, o, t] = b[o] + Σc,k x[n, c, t+k] · w[o, c, k]
example:
import torch
from torch import nn

signal = torch.tensor([[[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]]], device="cuda")
conv = nn.Conv1d(1, 1, kernel_size=3, bias=True).cuda()
with torch.no_grad():
    conv.weight.copy_(torch.tensor([[[0.5, -1, 2]]], device="cuda"))
    conv.bias.copy_(torch.tensor([0.25], device="cuda"))
result = conv(signal)
limitations: Fixed fixture: batch=1, one input/output channel, kernel width=3, stride=1, padding=0, dilation=1.
PyTorch Conv1d computes cross-correlation (the kernel is not reversed); the teaching kernel covers only this valid case.

tensors.name: signal
tensors.description: One batch, one channel, five time steps.

stages.title: Slide the receptive field
stages.summary: Output position t reads signal[t:t+3], pairing each sample with the same-ordered filter tap.
stages.insight: Unlike mathematical convolution, deep-learning Conv1d does not reverse filter order.

stages.title: Accumulate bias
stages.summary: The three products and scalar output-channel bias form one output value.
stages.insight: Each CUDA thread owns a distinct output position, so this fixture needs no synchronization.
